profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I'm a software engineer specializing in machine learning. I'm currently working at Google on state of the art AI techniques to block bots from abusing websites as credit card fraud, account takeovers, and scraping. I'm focused on improving the ground truth data in reCAPTCHA, which is used to evaluate the performance of the real-time detection engine. 

My past work was in systems integration and image processing. My biggest achievement was rewriting the almost all of the production line software at a multi-million dollar industrial facility (Jeep Wrangler assembly plant), which involved integrating diverse hardware and meeting strict uptime goals. 

I also worked on image processing and machine learning problems relevant to national security. I filed a unique patent for the GPS-denied navigation using military hardware, which reached the attention of the highest levels of the army and intelligence communities.

positions.title: Software Engineer (L5)
positions.description: reCAPTCHA machine learning: evaluation of ground truth for billions of sessions, novel detection rules for bots, statistics and data analysis

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: I have additional responsibilities with my new title, which includes providing guidance to other programmers. In addition to programming in Python, C++, and Matlab, I've also been using Docker and AWS to deploy programs at scale in a secure cloud (govcloud).

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer 2
positions.description:
I'm doing research in image processing at a defense contractor. Mix of Matlab, Python, C++. 

Programming projects:
- Underground Facilities Analysis Center (UFAC) Automated Assessment of Targets and Defense (A2TD) - I wrote Python and C++ code to find and characterize underground facilities in a secure computing environment. I worked on weaponeering portal and tunnel structures after fitting them to LIDAR scans.
- FINDER - I wrote Matlab and Python code to automatically locate photographs anywhere in the world using terrain skylines.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
I'm a programmer at the Jeep Wrangler automotive assembly line (TSAP). My code is responsible for millions of dollars of automotive production every year at TSAP and JNAP tier 1 suppliers in Detroit.

Programming projects:
• Custom HMIs for error proofing, quality inspection stations, vehicle repairs, and realtime measurements (mix of C++ and C#)
• MES Industrial automation and PLC communication (Wonderware QuickScript.NET scripts)
• Server programs for data gathering and analysis, RFID tracking, and pick to light systems (mostly C#)
• Internal productivity websites and webapps (Java/JSP)
• SAP integration through NCO/JCO APIs (C# and Java)

Recently Completed Projects 
• Saved over $80,000 per year by replacing a per-vehicle printed paper process with a new webapp and Wonderware scripts
• Saved over $20,000 by upgrading our production database from MSSQL 2000 to 2012
• Replaced the Andon scoreboards with a new productivity calculation system (FTC, JPH)
• Reduced downtime and prevented misbuilds by fixing many bugs in legacy code and implementing new production line stations and linestops
• Saved $10,000 in integration costs by doing an ETL process between databases to migrate our old access control system to a newer system
• Resolved $13,000 in OSHA violations for lack of documentation and auditing of lifting equipment by implementing a new electronic safety equipment inspection system, integrated with the production lines and automatically enforcing safety policies.

honors.title: Above and Beyond the Call of Duty (ABCD) Award
honors.description:
"David Johnson deserves this ABCD for his initiatives and thoroughness in preparing for a customer demo, his resourcefulness when things didn't go according to plan and his embodiment of ARA's core values (passion and service) with our customer. David's passion about meeting project objectives and providing excellent customer service is commendable, and he's made a big impact on the GPS-denied geolocation projected for NVESD as well as with the team that's working on the Finder project for NGA-Research."

Nominated by Dirk Warnaar, March 25, 2019.
honors.issuer: Issued by Applied Research Associates, Inc · Mar 2019

honors.title: Employee of the Year
honors.description: I was voted employee of the year among salary employees at the Toledo South Assembly Plant (TSAP). I received a bonus payment and a certificate, which reads, "Certificate of Appreciation. Exemplary Employee Award - David Johnson. For demonstrated dedication and professional conduct in carrying his management responsibilities in contributing to the present and future success of our organization. Hyundai MOBIS."

publications.title: Introduction to Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) for reCAPTCHA Classification

patents.title: GPS-denied geolocation
patents.description: Systems and techniques for navigation in a GPS-denied environment that do not rely on locations of known points. Instead, the operator can measure distance and/or inclination as well as azimuth to arbitrary points on the visual horizon (or sub-horizon) from their location. These observations can then be compared to precomputed distances and inclinations for corresponding azimuths to the visual horizon of a grid of points based on known surface terrain data. The closest grid point to the observer's location obtained in this way can be refined using a model of the surrounding environment, allowing for the operators position to be quickly and accurately determined.
